Staff at the front desk remembered my name by day two, which was a nice touch. Only downside was the wifi dropped a couple of times in the evening. Breakfast buffet had a good variety of South Indian and continental options.
Amazing experience overall, must visit.

Visited early morning around 7am to avoid the crowd, which worked out well — the gardens were quiet and well maintained, with clearly labeled plant species. There's a small entry fee that goes toward upkeep according to the signage. Restrooms near the entrance were clean but the ones further inside were locked. Good accessibility with ramps at the main gate.

Ticket counter had no clear queue system, a lot of pushing and confusion especially on the weekend we visited. Several informational plaques were faded and unreadable. Restrooms near the exit were locked with no staff around to help.

Went on a weekday and it wasn't crowded at all, could take my time at the viewpoint without people crowding for photos. The pathway up has decent lighting and railings for safety, though a few sections were under repair when I visited. Worth the entry fee just for the sunset view.

Signage is only in Hindi and English, so it might be tricky for other tourists. Ticket counter had a short queue around noon. Wheelchair access exists but only at the ground floor.
Everything was absolutely perfect, couldn't have asked for a better visit, no complaints at all.
